title: The Favor That Was Never Requested
title_ja: 頼まれていなかった手助け
fact_notes: オリジナル教材。一般原理を扱う架空の事例・論説。実際の組織、調査、実証結果ではない。台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A group of students is preparing for a science fair at school.
sentences.ja: 生徒の班が学校の科学発表会の準備をしている。

sentences.en: Each member is responsible for a different part of the display.
sentences.ja: 各班員は展示の異なる部分を担当する。

sentences.en: One student, Noah, notices that his partner's chart contains several unfinished sections.
sentences.ja: ノアは相手の図表に未完成部分がいくつかあることに気づく。

sentences.en: He decides to complete them himself without discussing the changes with his partner.
sentences.ja: 相手と変更を相談せず自分で完成させることを決める。

sentences.en: The next morning, his partner is surprised to find that the chart has been changed.
sentences.ja: 翌朝相手は図表が変更されたことに驚く。

sentences.en: She explains that she had left the sections empty because she was waiting for the results of another experiment.
sentences.ja: 別の実験結果を待っていたので空欄にしていたと説明する。

sentences.en: Noah had interpreted the empty spaces as evidence that she needed assistance.
sentences.ja: ノアは空欄を彼女が援助を必要としている証拠と解釈していた。

sentences.en: His attempt to save time has created additional work for both students.
sentences.ja: 時間を節約しようとした試みが二人に追加作業を生んだ。

sentences.en: They discuss why their understanding of the situation differed.
sentences.ja: 状況理解が異なった理由を話し合う。

sentences.en: Noah explains that he was concerned about the approaching deadline.
sentences.ja: 締め切りが近づくことを心配したとノアは説明する。

sentences.en: His partner recognizes his intention but points out that she could have provided important information if he had asked.
sentences.ja: 相手は意図を認めるが、尋ねられていれば重要情報を提供できたと指摘する。

sentences.en: They agree to check with each other before making substantial changes to someone else's work.
sentences.ja: 他者の作業に大きな変更を加える前に互いに確認することに同意する。

sentences.en: The students also create a shared list showing tasks that have been completed and tasks that are waiting for further information.
sentences.ja: 完了済み作業と追加情報待ちの作業を示す共有一覧も作る。

sentences.en: This arrangement helps them distinguish unfinished work from work that cannot yet be completed.
sentences.ja: この仕組みは未完成の作業とまだ完成できない作業を区別する助けになる。

sentences.en: They continue offering assistance when another person encounters a difficulty.
sentences.ja: 他者が困難に直面すると援助を申し出ることは続ける。

sentences.en: However, they try to clarify what kind of assistance would actually be useful.
sentences.ja: しかし実際にどのような援助が役立つか明確にしようとする。

sentences.en: Helping someone involves more than recognizing a possible problem.
sentences.ja: 人を助けるには問題の可能性に気づく以上のことが伴う。

sentences.en: It also involves listening to the person whose work or circumstances will be affected.
sentences.ja: 仕事や事情が影響を受ける人の話を聞くことも伴う。

sentences.en: A well-intended action may become more useful when it is based on a shared understanding of the situation.
sentences.ja: 善意の行動も共有した状況理解に基づくとより有用になることがある。

sentences.en: Noah learns that asking a question can itself be a valuable form of assistance.
sentences.ja: 問いを尋ねること自体が価値ある援助になり得るとノアは学ぶ。

vocabulary.definition: state of being hard to do

questions.prompt: What is the group preparing for?
Why does Noah change the chart?
options: He thinks its empty sections indicate a need for help.
He knows the experiment has been canceled.
He has been told to replace the results.
His partner asked for a new chart.
questions.explanation_ja: 空欄を援助が必要な証拠と解釈。

questions.prompt: Why had the sections been left empty?
options: She did not know how to draw a chart.
She wanted to end the project.
She had already entered the final results elsewhere.
The partner was waiting for experimental results.
It ignores information that his partner possesses.
It takes place after the fair ends.
It is requested by the teacher.
questions.explanation_ja: 相手の情報を確認していない。

options: A lack of equipment in the laboratory.
Confirm major changes with the other person first.
Complete all charts before experiments begin.

questions.prompt: What does their shared list indicate?
options: The names of every science fair visitor.
Completed tasks and tasks waiting for information.
Only the dates of past experiments.
It means every unfinished task is unacceptable.
It removes the need for discussion.
It establishes that all tasks are equally difficult.
It helps them avoid confusing unavailable information with neglected work.
questions.explanation_ja: 情報待ちと未着手を区別。

options: Intended to help or do good.
Completing someone else's task is always the best way to help.
Helpful cooperation requires understanding what another person actually needs.
questions.explanation_ja: 相手の必要を確認する。
